item.title: My Learning Journey This Week
item.description:
What I did

For the last 2 weeks, I have been learning and trying out new things such as Python, Markdown, Blender, and right now Github under my parents supervision. Currently, I am writing this learning journal as an introduction exercise to VS Code and Github. Python

I practiced Python in two Jupyter notebooks called hellworld.ipynb and chemi.ipynb.

In hellworld.ipynb, I learned how to:

  • import libraries such as NumPy and Matplotlib
  • create variables and use scientific notation
  • calculate square roots
  • write and use functions
  • work with arrays
  • use loops and array ranges
  • create line plots with labels, colors, markers, and different line styles
  • plot mathematical functions such as sine waves

In chemi.ipynb, I applied Python to a chemistry problem. I modeled a reversible chemical reaction, where substances A and B change into C and D over time. I used arrays to store the time and concentrations, a loop to calculate the changes, and Matplotlib to plot the results.

The chemistry exercise was more challenging because I had to translate a mathematical equation into Python instructions. I learned that programming can be used to simulate real-world processes, not just perform simple calculations. I also learned that errors are part of programming and can help me find what needs to be fixed.

Blender

I also worked on a Blender project called Jeentuh2.blend. I modeled a donut shape and added icing that drips over the sides. The most challenging part was shaping the icing so that the drips looked natural. I learned how 3D modeling can turn simple shapes into a more detailed object.

Github

I learned how to use GitHub to manage my code and projects. I created a repository for my learning journal and pushed my changes from VS Code. I also learned how to create branches, make commits, and merge changes. This helps me keep track of my work and collaborate with others in the future.

What I enjoyed

I really liked learning the basics of Python. It was exciting and incredibely interesting to basically learn another language to talk to literal computers. Its really crazy when you think about it. The Blender project was also really fun. Sculpting my own donut esepcially making the icing was really fun. It felt really smooth throughout the process. Since i like writing, writing this learning journal has also been quite enjoyable.

What was challenging

Of course I also had my share of problems throughtout the projects. For example, when my father gave me quite the challenging chemistry exercise to solve in python. I think it took me 2 whole days to finally solve it. And not by myself but with help from my sister. I think my main problem was that I had just been introduced to all this new information about chemistry and python, which lead me to quickly get furstrated and honestly give up at heart. My blender project went pretty smoothly, but I did struggle for a short time with Github, but I think I was just overthinking it.

What’s next?

My last goal for the summer break is creating a website purely about me. Ive got about 3 more days time to finish until my summer break ends. So I have to focus on the website now.

End/What I think I have improved over the 2 weeks

I think this is a good time to end my learning journal. Looking back, I think I have learned a lot of new things and I am proud of myself for going through with all these challenges. I think I have also learned a lot about myself and how I can efficiently learn new things instead of getting stuck. I also think that I will be able to apply all these skills in the future, especially in my schoolwork and group projects. Goodbye and maybe see you in the future.

item.title: Python, Data, and a Donut Plot
item.description:
What I did

I connected Python to my Quarto journal and used it to generate a donut plot. I made up a small set of summer activity data so I could see how a list of numbers becomes a visual story.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

activities = ["Coding", "Reading", "Design", "Breaks"]
hours = [8, 5, 3, 4]
colors = ["#2a6f97", "#61a5c2", "#f4a261", "#e9c46a"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.pie(
    hours,
    labels=activities,
    colors=colors,
    autopct="%1.0f%%",
    startangle=90,
    wedgeprops={"width": 0.38, "edgecolor": "white"},
)
ax.set_title("My Summer Project Time")
ax.set_aspect("equal")
plt.show()

What I learned

The activities list supplies the labels, and the hours list supplies the sizes. Matplotlib matches the items by position: the first label goes with the first number, and so on.

The donut shape comes from wedgeprops. Setting width below 1 leaves a hole in the middle of the pie. autopct adds percentages automatically, which makes the chart easier to read than a list of numbers.

Why this connects

Python is not only for calculations. It can also turn information into something I can inspect quickly. The chart makes it obvious that coding takes the biggest share of this example, while still showing how the other activities fit around it.

Next

I want to replace the sample numbers with real data from a week of my project and compare the chart with what I expected before I measured it.

item.title: Signal in the Summer
item.description:
Signal in the Summer

An original song

Verse 1

Wake up to a window full of gold
A brand-new question waiting to be told
I do not need to know the whole way through
I just need one small thing to try and do

Pre-chorus

Every wrong turn leaves a little light
Every messy draft gets closer to right

Chorus

I am finding my signal in the summer
Turning little sparks into a sound
I can ask for help and still discover
The best ideas are the ones I build out loud
Step by step, beat by beat
There is something new beneath my feet

Verse 2

Code on the screen, a rhythm in my head
A thousand possibilities ahead
I will keep the parts that feel like me
And let the rest become a better melody

Bridge

No shortcut, no perfect line
Just a curious heart and a little time
If the answer hides, I will start again
That is how a question becomes a friend

Final chorus

I am finding my signal in the summer
Turning little sparks into a sound
I can ask for help and still discover
The best ideas are the ones I build out loud
Step by step, beat by beat
I am making something that is me

Note

I wrote this about learning with AI while keeping my own ideas in the driver’s seat. The song is mine because I chose the theme, shaped the lyrics, and revised the parts that did not sound like me.
